steps.message:
You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Task Description:
You are the bioinformatician of a cancer-genomics core facility. Tumour and normal DNA of three
patients was sequenced on a small hybrid-capture panel. The clinical team needs, for every patient,
the tumour/normal pair and the somatic variants of the tumour.

Task directory:
- `/task`

Inputs (read-only) under `/task/input`:
- `fastq/<sample_id>_R1.fastq.gz`, `fastq/<sample_id>_R2.fastq.gz` - paired-end reads (2 x 100 nt),
  one pair of files per library (six libraries)
- `manifest.tsv` - sample sheet exported from the LIMS: `patient`, `sample_type` (`tumour` or
  `normal`), `sample_id`, `fastq_1`, `fastq_2`
- `reference/ref.fa` (+ `.fai`) - the panel reference, one contig (`chr22_panel`); no aligner index is
  provided
- `targets.bed` - the capture targets on the panel reference (0-based, half-open)
- `core_notes.md` - hand-over notes of the sequencing core

Available software (on `PATH`): `bwa`, `minimap2`, `samtools`, `bcftools` (with `bgzip`, `tabix`),
Python 3.12 with `pysam`, numpy, scipy and pandas. There is no internet access.

Your task:
1. Align the reads of every library to the panel reference.
2. Establish, for every patient, which normal library was prepared from the same individual as the
   patient's tumour library.
3. Call the somatic single-nucleotide variants and short insertions/deletions of every tumour
   inside the capture targets.

Required outputs under `/task/output`:
- `pairing.tsv` - tab-separated with the columns `patient`, `tumour_sample`, `normal_sample`; one
  row per patient of the manifest. `tumour_sample` is the `sample_id` of the patient's tumour
  library as listed in the manifest; `normal_sample` is the `sample_id` of the normal library that
  comes from the same individual as that tumour library.
- `somatic/<patient>.vcf.gz` - one gzip- or bgzip-compressed VCF per patient holding the somatic
  variants of that patient's tumour library.
  - A somatic variant is a single-nucleotide variant or short insertion/deletion that is present in
    tumour cells of the patient and absent from the patient's germline. Germline variants, and
    differences from the reference that arise during library preparation, sequencing or read
    alignment, are not somatic variants.
  - Reported variants have `FILTER` = `PASS`; records with any other FILTER value are not part of
    the deliverable.
  - `CHROM`, `POS`, `REF`, `ALT` follow the VCF specification relative to `reference/ref.fa`; one
    alternate allele per record; insertions and deletions left-aligned and parsimonious (the
    representation `bcftools norm` produces).
  - Every record carries `AF=<number>` in the `INFO` column: the fraction (0-1) of the tumour
    library's DNA fragments covering the site that carry the alternate allele.
  - The reporting range of the assay starts at an allele fraction of 5%; variants below it may be
    left out.
- `summary.json` - `{"patients": {"<patient>": {"tumour_sample": "<sample_id>", "normal_sample":
  "<sample_id>", "n_snv": <int>, "n_indel": <int>}, ...}}` where `n_snv` and `n_indel` are the
  numbers of `PASS` single-nucleotide and insertion/deletion records in that patient's VCF and the
  two sample ids repeat `pairing.tsv`.

Constraints:
- Do not modify anything under `/task/input`; write deliverables only under `/task/output`.
- Extra columns, INFO fields and sample columns are allowed.
- Do not ask for confirmation. Execute directly.

steps.message:
Analysis: Tools are recent (bwa 0.7.19, samtools/bcftools 1.25, pysam 0.24.1). Six libraries with ~46-49k read pairs for tumours and ~23-25k for normals (matches 180x/90x on 46 kb). Read names show flow cell 214 / lane 2 and indexes matching the notes. /task/software has only a README to check.
Plan: Check README, then create a writable work directory /task/work (deliverables only in /task/output). Copy the reference, build bwa index, and align all six libraries: bwa mem -> fixmate -> sort by name -> markdup -> sort coordinate -> index. Then inspect coverage over targets.

arguments.keystrokes: cat /task/software/README.txt
mkdir -p /task/work/bam && cd /task/work && cp /task/input/reference/ref.fa /task/input/reference/ref.fa.fai . 2>/dev/null; ls -la /task/input/reference/
cd /task/work && bwa index ref.fa 2>&1 | tail -2

cat > /task/work/align.sh << 'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
IN=/task/input
W=/task/work
cd $W
for s in CG24-4187 CG24-7410 CG24-9024 CG24-1366 CG24-6425 CG24-3973; do
  R1=$IN/fastq/${s}_R1.fastq.gz
  R2=$IN/fastq/${s}_R2.fastq.gz
  bwa mem -t 4 -R "@RG\tID:$s\tSM:$s\tPL:ILLUMINA\tLB:$s\tPU:HKF3WDSX7.2" $R1 $R2 2> $W/${s}.bwa.log \
   | samtools fixmate -m -@ 2 -O bam - - 2> /dev/null \
   | samtools sort -@ 2 -n -o $W/${s}.qsort.bam
  samtools markdup -@ 2 -f $W/${s}.markdup.metrics.txt $W/${s}.qsort.bam $W/${s}.tmp.bam
  samtools sort -@ 2 -o $W/bam/$s.bam $W/${s}.tmp.bam
  samtools index $W/bam/$s.bam
  rm -f $W/${s}.qsort.bam $W/${s}.tmp.bam
  samtools flagstat -@ 2 $W/bam/$s.bam > $W/${s}.flagstat.txt
  echo done $s
done
EOF
chmod +x /task/work/align.sh; echo ok
bash /task/work/align.sh 2>&1 | tail -20

Plan: Fix align.sh to include `ref.fa` before the FASTQ files, then run the alignment for all six libraries. Afterwards check flagstat, duplicate rates and coverage on target.

set -euo pipefail

for s in CG24-4187 CG24-7410 CG24-9024 CG24-1366 CG24-6425 CG24-3973; do

  samtools flagstat -@ 2 $W/bam/$s.bam > $W/${s}.flagstat.txt
  echo done $s
done
EOF

steps.message:
Analysis: samtools markdup requires coordinate-sorted input (with fixmate -m). My use of `-Q`/queryname sorting was wrong. Simplify: bwa mem -> fixmate -m -> coordinate sort -> markdup -> index.
Plan: Rewrite the pipeline as: bwa mem | samtools fixmate -m -u | samtools sort -o ssort.bam | samtools markdup -s -f metrics ssort.bam bam/s.bam, then index. Run for all six libraries and inspect flagstat + markdup metrics + coverage.

cat > /task/work/align.sh << 'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
IN=/task/input
W=/task/work
cd $W
mkdir -p tmp bam
for s in CG24-4187 CG24-7410 CG24-9024 CG24-1366 CG24-6425 CG24-3973; do
  R1=$IN/fastq/${s}_R1.fastq.gz
  R2=$IN/fastq/${s}_R2.fastq.gz
  bwa mem -t 4 -R "@RG\tID:$s\tSM:$s\tPL:ILLUMINA\tLB:$s\tPU:HKF3WDSX7.2" ref.fa $R1 $R2 2> $W/${s}.bwa.log \
   | samtools fixmate -m -@ 2 -O bam - $W/${s}.fix.bam
  samtools sort -@ 2 -m 512M -o $W/${s}.csort.bam $W/${s}.fix.bam
  samtools markdup -@ 2 -s -T $W/tmp/$s -f $W/${s}.markdup.metrics.txt $W/${s}.csort.bam $W/bam/$s.bam
  samtools index $W/bam/$s.bam
  rm -f $W/${s}.fix.bam $W/${s}.csort.bam
  samtools flagstat -@ 2 $W/bam/$s.bam > $W/${s}.flagstat.txt
  echo done $s
done
EOF
bash /task/work/align.sh 2>&1 | tail -15

Analysis: gtcheck needs a query genotype file; I got none with `-g`. Genotypes show shared hets (e.g. CG24-3973 & CG24-9024 both 0/1 at 3830 and 14371), which suggests same-individual pairs. I'll compute a proper pairwise concordance matrix myself.

arguments.keystrokes: cd /task/work && bcftools query -l germline.vcf.gz > samples.txt && bcftools view -v snps -m2 -M2 -Q 30 germline.vcf.gz | bcftools query -f '%POS[\t%GT]\n' > gt_snps.tsv && wc -l gt_snps.tsv

cat > /task/work/pairing.py << 'EOF'
import itertools, sys
samples=[l.strip() for l in open('/task/work/samples.txt')]
rows=[]
for line in open('/task/work/gt_snps.tsv'):
    f=line.rstrip('\n').split('\t')
    pos=f[0]; gts=f[1:]
    rows.append((pos,gts))
code={'0/0':0,'0/1':1,'1/1':2,'./.':-1}
print('sites',len(rows),'samples',samples)
# informative sites: at least one sample non-ref
cnt=0
for pos,gts in rows:
    if any(g!='0/0' for g in gts): cnt+=1
print('informative sites (any variant):',cnt)
n=len(samples)
for a,b in itertools.combinations(range(n),2):
    agree=disc=miss=0
    for pos,gts in rows:
        ga,gb=code[gts[a]],code[gts[b]]
        if ga<0 or gb<0: miss+=1; continue
        if ga==gb: agree+=1
        else: disc+=1
    tot=agree+disc
    print(f'{samples[a]} vs {samples[b]}: agree={agree} discordant={disc} rate={agree/tot:.4f}' if tot else 'na')
EOF
python3 /task/work/pairing.py

Analysis: Pairwise genotype concordance over 155 biallelic SNP sites shows clear best matches: CG24-4187 (tumour PT-0452) with CG24-1366 (0.87), CG24-7410 (tumour PT-0740) with CG24-6425 (0.86), CG24-9024 (tumour PT-0760) with CG24-3973 (0.83). This means two of the manifest's normals are swapped. Concordance for manifest pairs 4187/6425 (0.50) and 7410/1366 (0.49) is at unrelated level. I should confirm with a stricter metric (opposite-homozygote/IBS0 counts at high-depth sites and AF-based evidence) before finalising.
Plan: 1) Use pysam to build a per-site DP/AF matrix at the germline variant sites (all 6 samples, DP>=30) and compute IBS0 counts per pair plus AF agreement at sites where one sample is clearly het/hom. 2) Then move to somatic calling with the established pairing.

cat > /task/work/pairing2.py << 'EOF'
import pysam, itertools
vcf=pysam.VariantFile('/task/work/germline.vcf.gz')
samples=list(vcf.header.samples)
print(samples)
data=[]
for rec in vcf:
    if len(rec.ref)!=1 or any(len(a)!=1 for a in rec.alts): continue
    dps=[];afs=[];gts=[]
    ok=True
    for s in samples:
        f=rec.samples[s]
        gt=f.get('GT',(None,))
        dp=f.get('DP') or 0
        ad=f.get('AD') or ()
        if dp<25: ok=False
        alt=sum(ad[1:]) if len(ad)>1 else 0
        af=alt/dp if dp else 0.0
        dps.append(dp);afs.append(af);gts.append(''.join(str(x) for x in gt if x is not None))
    if ok:
        data.append((rec.pos,dps,afs,gts))
print('sites with all DP>=25:',len(data))
def cl(af):
    if af<0.10: return 0
    if af<0.80: return 1
    return 2
n=len(samples)
print('pair  IBS0  discordant  concordant')
for a,b in itertools.combinations(range(n),2):
    ibs0=disc=agree=0
    for pos,dps,afs,gts in data:
        ca,cb=cl(afs[a]),cl(afs[b])
        if ca==cb: agree+=1
        else:
            disc+=1
            if {ca,cb}=={0,2}: ibs0+=1
    print(f'{samples[a]}-{samples[b]}: agree={agree} disc={disc} IBS0={ibs0}')
EOF

import pysam, numpy as np, pickle, sys, os
CONTIG='chr22_panel'; W='/task/work'
fa=pysam.FastaFile(W+'/ref.fa'); refseq=fa.fetch(CONTIG).upper()
L=len(refseq)
idx=np.full(L,-1,dtype=np.int64)
k=0
for line in open('/task/input/targets.bed'):
    f=line.split(); s,e=int(f[1]),int(f[2])
    idx[s:e]=np.arange(k,k+(e-s)); k+=(e-s)
nS=k
print('target sites',nS)
BASE=np.full(256,-1,dtype=np.int64)
for i,c in enumerate('ACGT'):
    BASE[ord(c)]=i; BASE[ord(c.lower())]=i
FLAGS=pysam.FUNMAP|pysam.FSECONDARY|pysam.FQCFAIL|pysam.FDUP|pysam.FSUPPLEMENTARY
MINBQ=20; MINMQ=20
samples=[l.strip() for l in open(W+'/samples.txt')]
out={}
for s in samples:
    bam=pysam.AlignmentFile(f'{W}/bam/{s}.bam')
    acc=np.zeros(nS*8,dtype=np.int64)   # site*(8) + base*2 + strand
    dep=np.zeros(nS,dtype=np.int64)     # all aligned bases (any bq)
    indels={}
    nread=0
    for r1,r2 in [ (None,None) ]:
        pass
    for read in bam.fetch(CONTIG):
        if read.is_unmapped or read.is_secondary or read.is_supplementary or read.is_qcfail or read.is_duplicate: continue
        if read.mapping_quality<MINMQ: continue
        nread+=1
        strand=1 if read.is_reverse else 0
        qp=[]; rp=[]
        for q,r in read.get_aligned_pairs(matches_only=True):
            if r is not None: qp.append(q); rp.append(r)
        if qp:
            qp=np.asarray(qp,dtype=np.int64); rp=np.asarray(rp,dtype=np.int64)
            seq=np.frombuffer(read.query_sequence.encode(),dtype=np.uint8)[qp]
            qual=np.asarray(read.query_qualities,dtype=np.int64)[qp]
            b=BASE[seq]
            si=idx[rp]
            ok=(si>=0)&(b>=0)
            np.add.at(dep, si[ok], 1)
            ok2=ok&(qual>=MINBQ)
            np.add.at(acc, si[ok2]*8+b[ok2]*2+strand, 1)
        # indels
        rpos=read.reference_start; qpos=read.query_start
        cig=read.cigartuples
        seqstr=read.query_sequence
        for op,l in cig:
            if op==0:
                rpos+=l; qpos+=l
            elif op==1:
                ins=seqstr[qpos:qpos+l]
                p=rpos
                while l>0 and p>0 and ins[-1]==refseq[p-1]:
                    ins=ins[-1]+ins[:-1]; p-=1
                key=('I',p,l)
                d=indels.setdefault(key,[set(),0,0])
                d[0].add(read.query_name); d[1 if strand else 2]+=1
                qpos+=l
            elif op==2:
                dele=refseq[rpos:rpos+l]
                p=rpos
                while l>0 and p>0 and dele[-1]==refseq[p-1]:
                    dele=dele[-1]+dele[:-1]; p-=1
                key=('D',p,l)
                d=indels.setdefault(key,[set(),0,0])
                d[0].add(read.query_name); d[1 if strand else 2]+=1
                rpos+=l
            elif op==4: qpos+=l
            elif op==5: rpos+=l
            elif op==3: rpos+=l; qpos+=l
            else: pass
    indels_s={('%s|%d|%d'%(t,p,l)):[len(v),f,r] for (t,p,l),(v,f,r) in indels.items()}
    out[s]={'acc':acc,'dep':dep,'indels':indels_s,'nread':nread}
    print(s,'reads',nread,'indel keys',len(indels_s), flush=True)
    np.save(W+f'/acc_{s}.npy', acc); np.save(W+f'/dep_{s}.npy', dep)
    pickle.dump(indels_s, open(W+f'/indels_{s}.pkl','wb'))
print('done')

import pysam, numpy as np, pickle

fa=pysam.FastaFile(W+'/ref.fa'); refseq=fa.fetch(CONTIG).upper()

for line in open('/task/input/targets.bed'):

    idx[s:e]=np.arange(k,k+(e-s)); tpos.extend(range(s,e)); k+=(e-s)
nS=k

np.save(W+'/tpos.npy',tpos)
BASE=np.full(256,-1,dtype=np.int64)
for i,c in enumerate('ACGT'):
    BASE[ord(c)]=i; BASE[ord(c.lower())]=i
MINBQ=20; MINMQ=20

def canon_del(p,seq):
    while len(seq)>0 and p>0 and seq[-1]==refseq[p-1]:
        seq=seq[-1]+seq[:-1]; p-=1
    while len(seq)>0 and p+len(seq)<L and seq[0]==refseq[p+len(seq)]:
        seq=seq[1:]
    return p,seq
def canon_ins(p,ins):
    while len(ins)>0 and p>0 and ins[-1]==refseq[p-1]:
        ins=ins[-1]+ins[:-1]; p-=1
    while len(ins)>0 and p<L and ins[0]==refseq[p]:
        ins=ins[1:]
    return p,ins

samples=[l.strip() for l in open(W+'/samples.txt')]
for s in samples:
    bam=pysam.AlignmentFile(f'{W}/bam/{s}.bam')
    acc=np.zeros(nS*8,dtype=np.int64)
    dep=np.zeros(nS,dtype=np.int64)
    indels={}
    nread=0
    for read in bam.fetch(CONTIG):
        if read.is_unmapped or read.is_secondary or read.is_supplementary or read.is_qcfail or read.is_duplicate: continue
        if read.mapping_quality<MINMQ: continue
        nread+=1
        strand=1 if read.is_reverse else 0
        pairs=read.get_aligned_pairs(matches_only=False)
        qs=read.query_sequence
        prev_r=None
        i=0
        while i<len(pairs):
            q,r=pairs[i]
            if q is not None and r is not None:
                if 0<=r<L:
                    j=idx[r]
                    if j>=0:
                        dep[j]+=1
                        b=BASE[ord(qs[q])]
                        if b>=0 and read.query_qualities[q]>=MINBQ:
                            acc[j*8+b*2+strand]+=1
                prev_r=r; i+=1
            elif q is not None and r is None:
                st=i
                chars=[]
                while i<len(pairs) and pairs[i][1] is None and pairs[i][0] is not None:
                    chars.append(qs[pairs[i][0]]); i+=1
                ins=''.join(chars)
                p=(prev_r+1) if prev_r is not None else read.reference_start
                p,ins=canon_ins(p,ins)
                key=('I',p,len(ins),ins)
                d=indels.setdefault(key,[set(),0,0])
                d[0].add(read.query_name)
                d[1+strand]+=1
            elif q is None and r is not None:
                st=i
                while i<len(pairs) and pairs[i][0] is None and pairs[i][1] is not None:
                    i+=1
                p=pairs[st][1]; dl=i-st
                seq=refseq[p:p+dl]
                p,seq=canon_del(p,seq)
                key=('D',p,len(seq),seq)
                d=indels.setdefault(key,[set(),0,0])
                d[0].add(read.query_name)
                d[1+strand]+=1
                prev_r=pairs[i-1][1]
            else:
                i+=1
    ser={('|'.join(map(str,k))):[len(v),f,r] for k,(v,f,r) in indels.items()}
    np.save(W+f'/acc_{s}.npy',acc); np.save(W+f'/dep_{s}.npy',dep)
    pickle.dump(ser,open(W+f'/indels_{s}.pkl','wb'))
    print(s,'reads',nread,'indel keys',len(ser),flush=True)
print('done')

        qp=pairs[:,0]; rp=pairs[:,1]
        ci=cidx[rp]

        sq=np.frombuffer(read.query_sequence.encode(),dtype=np.uint8)
        qs=np.array(read.query_qualities,dtype=np.int64)
        bases=BASE[sq[qp]]
        bqs=qs[qp]
        relpos=qp if not read.is_reverse else (read.query_length-1-qp)
        for k in range(len(ci)):

import pickle, numpy as np, pysam
W='/task/work'
samples=[l.strip() for l in open(W+'/samples.txt')]
tp=np.load(W+'/tpos.npy'); cand=pickle.load(open(W+'/cand.pkl','wb'))['cand']
fa=pysam.FastaFile(W+'/ref.fa'); refseq=fa.fetch('chr22_panel').upper()
B='ACGT'
acc={s:np.load(f'{W}/acc_{s}.npy').reshape(-1,4,2) for s in samples}
p2={s:pickle.load(open(W+f'/p2_{s}.pkl','rb')) for s in samples}
refb=np.array([B.index(refseq[p]) for p in tp])
pairs={'CG24-4187':'CG24-1366','CG24-7410':'CG24-6425','CG24-9024':'CG24-3973'}
names={s:s[-4:] for s in samples}
def frag_depth(s, sitepos):
    spans=p2[s]['spans']
    c=0
    for f,rs,re_,st,mq in spans:
        if rs<=sitepos<re_: c+=1
    return c
def site_detail(s,k):
    recs=[r for r in p2[s]['recs'] if r[0]==k]
    return recs
for tum,norm in pairs.items():
    print('#'*20, tum, 'vs', norm)
    for m,k in enumerate(cand):
        p=int(tp[k]); rb=refb[k]
        a_t=acc[tum][k]; a_n=acc[norm][k]
        tot_t=a_t.sum(); tot_n=a_n.sum()
        alt_t=tot_t-a_t[rb]; alt_n=tot_n-a_n[rb]
        if alt_t<3: continue
        # other samples
        oth=''
        for s in samples:
            if s in (tum,norm): continue
            a=acc[s][k]; t=a.sum(); al=t-a[rb]
            oth+=f'{names[s]}:{al}/{t} '
        recs=site_detail(tum,k)
        # determine dominant alt base
        cnts={b:sum(1 for r in recs if r[2]==b and r[3]==1 and r[4]>=20)+0 for b in range(4)}
        altbase=max([b for b in range(4) if b!=rb], key=lambda b: sum(1 for r in recs if r[2]==b))
        ar=[r for r in recs if r[2]==altbase and r[4]>=20]
        f_fwd=sum(1 for r in ar if r[3]==0); f_rev=len(ar)-f_fwd
        bq=np.mean([r[4] for r in ar]) if ar else 0
        rp=np.mean([r[5] for r in ar]) if ar else 0
        frags=len(set(r[1] for r in ar))
        ctx=refseq[max(0,p-4):p+5]
        print(f'{p+1:7d} {B[rb]}>{B[altbase]} ctx={ctx} T_alt={alt_t:3d}/{tot_t:3d}={alt_t/max(1,tot_t):.3f} fragsAF={frags}/{frag_depth(tum,p)} N={alt_n:3d}/{tot_n:3d}={alt_n/max(1,tot_n):.3f} strand={f_fwd}/{f_rev} bq={bq:.1f} relpos={rp:.0f} | {oth}')

import pickle, numpy as np, pysam
W='/task/work'
samples=[l.strip() for l in open(W+'/samples.txt')]
tp=np.load(W+'/tpos.npy'); n=len(tp)
fa=pysam.FastaFile(W+'/ref.fa'); refseq=fa.fetch('chr22_panel').upper()
B='ACGT'; refb=np.array([B.index(refseq[p]) for p in tp])
cand=pickle.load(open(W+'/cand.pkl','rb'))['cand']
acc={s:np.load(f'{W}/acc_{s}.npy').reshape(-1,4,2) for s in samples}
p2={s:pickle.load(open(W+f'/p2_{s}.pkl','rb')) for s in samples}
fd={}
for s in samples:
    sp=np.array([(x[1],x[2]) for x in p2[s]['spans']],dtype=np.int64)
    fd[s]=(np.sort(sp[:,0]),np.sort(sp[:,1]))
def fragdepth(s,p):
    a,b=fd[s]
    return int(np.searchsorted(a,p,'right')-np.searchsorted(b,p,'left'))
bysite={}
for s in samples:
    d={}
    for r in p2[s]['recs']:
        d.setdefault(r[0],[]).append(r)
    bysite[s]=d
out=open(W+'/snv_table.tsv','w')
hdr=['sample','pos','ref','alt','refbasecount','altbasecount','totalbase','altbases','altfrags','fragdepth','fwd','rev','meanbq','minbq','meanrelpos','minrelpos','maxrelpos']
out.write('\t'.join(hdr)+'\n')
for m,k in enumerate(cand):
    p=int(tp[k]); rb=refb[k]
    for s in samples:
        a=acc[s][k]; tot=int(a.sum()); refcnt=int(a[rb].sum())
        recs=bysite[s].get(m,[])
        for b in range(4):
            if b==rb: continue
            cnt=int(a[b].sum())
            if cnt==0: continue
            ar=[r for r in recs if r[2]==b and r[4]>=20]
            frags=len(set(r[1] for r in ar))
            fwd=sum(1 for r in ar if r[3]==0); rev=len(ar)-fwd
            bqs=[r[4] for r in ar]; rps=[r[5] for r in ar]
            out.write('\t'.join(map(str,[s,p+1,B[rb],B[b],refcnt,cnt,tot,frags,fragdepth(s,p),fwd,rev,
                round(np.mean(bqs),1) if bqs else 0, min(bqs) if bqs else 0,
                round(np.mean(rps),1) if rps else 0, min(rps) if rps else 0, max(rps) if rps else 0]))+'\n')
out.close()
print('snv table done')
# indel table
ind={s:pickle.load(open(W+f'/indels_{s}.pkl','rb')) for s in samples}
keys=set()
for s in samples: keys.update(ind[s].keys())
o2=open(W+'/indel_table.tsv','w')
o2.write('key\tsample\ttype\tpos0\tlen\tseq\taltfrags\tfragdepth\tfwd\trev\n')
allkeys=[]
for s in samples:
    for kk in ind[s]: allkeys.append(kk)
for kk in sorted(keys):
    t,p0,l,seq=kk.split('|')
    p0=int(p0)
    for s in samples:
        v=ind[s].get(kk)
        if v is None: continue
        f,fr,rv=v
        o2.write('\t'.join(map(str,[kk,s,t,p0,l,seq,f,fragdepth(s,min(p0,max(0,p0-1)) if p0>0 else 0),fr,rv]))+'\n')
o2.close()
print('indel table done')
PYEOF

import pandas as pd

cols=['sample','pos','ref','alt','refcnt','altcnt','tot','altfrags','fragdepth','fwd','rev','meanbq','minbq','meanrelpos','minrelpos','maxrelpos']
df=pd.read_csv(W+'/snv_table.tsv',sep='\t',names=cols,header=0)

pairs={'PT-0452':('CG24-4187','CG24-1366'),'PT-0740':('CG24-7410','CG24-6425'),'PT-0760':('CG24-9024','CG24-3973')}

Analysis: Important discovery: pysam's query_name includes the mate field (" 1:N:0" vs " 2:N:0"), so my "fragment" counts were actually per-read counts. The deliverable requires fragment-level AF. Also, mate-level discordance is a great artifact detector (sequencing errors affect single reads, real variants affect all reads of a fragment). I'll rewrite the counting pass keyed by proper fragment ids (name without the mate field), recording per-fragment base support and indel support, plus fragment depth.
Plan: Write pass3.py: for each sample, iterate reads (non-dup, MQ>=20), group by fragment id; for candidate SNV sites record per-fragment per-mate base+BQ; for indels record per-fragment canonical events; also record per-fragment covered reference spans for depth. Store pickles. Then compute fragment AFs and mate-concordance statistics for tumour-only low-AF sites to see whether artifacts are per-read errors.

steps.message:
Analysis: Fragment-level data is now stored per sample in frag_<sample>.pkl (fragment id = first QNAME token, mates 'f'/'r', per-mate base calls with BQ and read position at candidate sites, canonical indel events, fragment span). My earlier per-read counts inflated support numbers roughly 2x, so AF must be recomputed at fragment level. The low-AF tumour-only sites in the FFPE library (CG24-9024) look enriched for C>T/G>A changes, which hints at deamination artifacts, while sites supported by both mates of a fragment are more likely real.
Plan: Write fragtable.py: for every candidate SNV site and every sample compute fragment-level numbers: depth (fragments whose span covers the site), alt fragments, fragments with both mates covering and both agreeing (concordant) vs single-mate alt (discordant), strand split, mean/min BQ, mean/min/max read position of the alt, and the reference context. Dump a TSV. Then print, for each tumour/normal pair, tumour-only sites (normal alt fragments = 0) sorted by tumour fragment AF, to find a clean separation between somatic variants and artifacts.

import pickle, numpy as np, pysam
W='/task/work'
samples=[l.strip() for l in open(W+'/samples.txt')]
tp=np.load(W+'/tpos.npy')
candk=pickle.load(open(W+'/cand.pkl','rb'))['cand']
cand=[int(tp[k]) for k in candk]
fa=pysam.FastaFile(W+'/ref.fa'); refseq=fa.fetch('chr22_panel').upper(); B='ACGT'
frag={s:pickle.load(open(W+f'/frag_{s}.pkl','rb')) for s in samples}
candpos={p:i for i,p in enumerate(sorted(set(cand)))}
rows=[]
for s in samples:
    fr=frag[s]
    for p in sorted(set(cand)):
        i=candpos[p]; rb=B.index(refseq[p])
        depth=0; alt=0; both=0; single=0; fwd=0; rev=0; bqs=[]; rps=[]
        for fid,d in fr.items():
            sp=d['span']
            coversF = 'f' in d['base'].get(i,{})
            coversR = 'r' in d['base'].get(i,{})
            if not (coversF or coversR):
                continue
            depth+=1
            calls=d['base'][i]
            ab=[calls[m] for m in calls if calls[m][0]!=rb]
            if ab:
                alt+=1
                for m,c in calls.items():
                    if c[0]==rb: continue
                    bqs.append(c[1]); rps.append(c[2])
                    if m=='f': fwd+=1
                    else: rev+=1
                nmat=sum(1 for m,c in calls.items() if c[0]!=rb)
                if nmat>=2: both+=1
                else:
                    # only one mate had a call at this site and it is alt; other mate may not cover
                    nocov=[m for m in ('f','r') if m not in calls]
                    if not nocov: single+=1   # other mate covered and agreed ref -> discordant fragment
        rows.append((s,p+1,refseq[p],depth,alt,both,single,fwd,rev,
                     round(np.mean(bqs),1) if bqs else 0,min(bqs) if bqs else 0,
                     round(np.mean(rps),1) if rps else 0))
import csv
with open(W+'/frag_snv.tsv','w',newline='') as fh:
    w=csv.writer(fh,delimiter='\t')
    w.writerow(['sample','pos','ref','depth','altfrag','both','discord','fwd','rev','meanbq','minbq','meanrp'])
    for r in rows: w.writerow(r)
print('rows',len(rows))
PYEOF

steps.message:
Analysis: Fragment structure verified: each fragment covers a candidate site with only one mate (insert size 260-280 bp, 100 bp reads, no overlap), so mate-concordance filtering is not usable; fragment AF = alt fragments / fragments covering the site. The SNV landscape is clear: germline (tumour≈normal≈0.5 or 1.0), reference-diffs (≈1.0 in all), noise (≤2%, low BQ, one-strand), and tumour-only sites forming clonal (≈purity/2) plus subclonal clusters down to ~5%. Indels are unambiguous: tumours have 5-7 events supported by 23-73 fragments, all other events are 1-4-fragment noise; normals have none.
Plan: Write pass4.py to aggregate indel events per sample with correct canonical (left-aligned, parsimonious) representation and fragment support/depth. Then write the final somatic caller that: (1) emits pairing.tsv, (2) per patient calls somatic SNVs (from frag pickles) and indels with filters AF>=0.05, >=4 alt fragments, normal support <=2 fragments, sanity strand check, (3) writes VCFs with INFO/AF, runs bcftools norm to guarantee representation, (4) writes summary.json.

import pysam, numpy as np, pickle, collections
W='/task/work'
samples=[l.strip() for l in open(W+'/samples.txt')]
fa=pysam.FastaFile(W+'/ref.fa'); refseq=fa.fetch('chr22_panel').upper(); L=len(refseq)
targets=[]
for line in open('/task/input/targets.bed'):
    f=line.split(); targets.append((int(f[1]),int(f[2])))
def in_target(p):
    return any(s<=p<e for s,e in targets)
def canon_ins(p,ins):
    # rotate left while last inserted base equals base before insertion point
    guard=0
    while p>0 and ins and ins[-1]==refseq[p-1] and guard<50:
        ins=ins[-1]+ins[:-1]; p-=1; guard+=1
    return p,ins
def canon_del(p,l):
    guard=0
    while p>0 and l>0 and refseq[p-1]==refseq[p+l-1] and guard<50:
        p-=1; guard+=1
    return p,refseq[p:p+l]
for s in samples:
    bam=pysam.AlignmentFile(f'{W}/bam/{s}.bam')
    frags=collections.defaultdict(lambda: {'indel':{}, 'span':[None,None]})
    for r in bam.fetch('chr22_panel'):
        if r.is_unmapped or r.is_secondary or r.is_supplementary or r.is_qcfail or r.is_duplicate: continue
        if r.mapping_quality<20: continue
        fid=r.query_name.split()[0]
        d=frags[fid]
        if d['span'][0] is None: d['span']=[r.reference_start,r.reference_end]
        else:
            d['span'][0]=min(d['span'][0],r.reference_start); d['span'][1]=max(d['span'][1],r.reference_end)
        rpos=r.reference_start; qpos=0; seqs=r.query_sequence
        for op,l in r.cigartuples:
            if op==0: rpos+=l; qpos+=l
            elif op==1:
                ins=seqs[qpos:qpos+l]
                p,ins=canon_ins(rpos,ins)
                if len(ins)<=8: d['indel'][('I',p,ins)]=d['indel'].get(('I',p,ins),0)+1
                qpos+=l
            elif op==2:
                p,dele=canon_del(rpos,l)
                if len(dele)<=8: d['indel'][('D',p,dele)]=d['indel'].get(('D',p,dele),0)+1
                rpos+=l
            elif op==4: qpos+=l
            elif op==5: rpos+=l
            elif op==3: rpos+=l; qpos+=l
    # aggregate
    ev=collections.defaultdict(lambda: {'frags':set(),'reads':0,'fwd':0,'rev':0})
    for fid,d in frags.items():
        for k,c in d['indel'].items():
            ev[k]['frags'].add(fid); ev[k]['reads']+=c
    # strand counts per event (from reads)
    res={}
    for k,d in ev.items():
        t,p,seq=k
        # depth: fragments whose span covers the event region
        if t=='D': lo,hi=p-1,p+len(seq)  # anchor base .. last deleted base inclusive
        else: lo,hi=p-1,p
        depth=0
        for fid,dd in frags.items():
            sp=dd['span']
            if sp[0]<=lo and sp[1]>=hi: depth+=1
        res[k]={'frags':len(d['frags']),'depth':depth,'reads':d['reads']}
    pickle.dump({'ev':{('|'.join(map(str,k))):v for k,v in res.items()},'nfrag':len(frags)},open(W+f'/indel_{s}.pkl','wb'))
    big=[(k,v) for k,v in res.items() if v['frags']>=4]
    print('==',s,'fragments',len(frags),'events>=4 frags:',len(big))
    for k,v in sorted(big,key=lambda x:-x[1]['frags']):
        t,p,seq=k

Analysis: I now have fragment-level AFs. Structure per tumour (normal-negative, other-library-negative sites): PT-0452: noise ≤0.024, then a band of ~12 sites at 0.097-0.25, then a clonal cluster ~0.30-0.39. PT-0740: noise ≤0.024, then band 0.043-0.29 (~16 sites), clonal ~0.29-0.33. PT-0760 (FFPE): band 0.05-0.30 with 28 sites of which 24 are C>T/G>A/C>A/G>T (deamination/oxidation signature) vs only 4-5 of 12-16 such types in the fresh tumours — indicating an FFPE artifact class on top of a real subclonal band. To decide whether the low-AF band is real subclonal somatic or generic noise, I'll test whether the three NORMAL libraries also carry private sites in the same AF band.
Plan: Write bandtest.py: for every sample, count private sites (alt fragments only in that sample, zero in the other five) in AF bands [0.03,0.05), [0.05,0.10), [0.10,0.20), [0.20,0.30), [0.30,0.60) with altfrag>=4, and list their substitution types. Comparing normals vs tumours will reveal whether a generic artifact process creates private low-AF sites.

import pandas as pd, numpy as np
W='/task/work'
cols=['sample','pos','ref','alt','refcnt','altcnt','tot','areads','areaddepth','fwd','rev','meanbq','minbq','meanrelpos','minrelpos','maxrelpos']
s=pd.read_csv(W+'/snv_table.tsv',sep='\t',names=cols,skiprows=1)
s=s.loc[s.groupby(['sample','pos']).altcnt.idxmax()][['sample','pos','ref','alt','fwd','rev']]
f=pd.read_csv(W+'/frag_snv.tsv',sep='\t')
f=f.merge(s,on=['sample','pos'],how='left')
f=f.dropna(subset=['alt']).copy()
f['af']=f.altfrag/f.depth
samples=sorted(f['sample'].unique())
piv=f.pivot_table(index=['pos','ref','alt'],columns='sample',values='altfrag').fillna(0)
dep=f.pivot_table(index=['pos','ref','alt'],columns='sample',values='depth').fillna(0)
rows=[]
for smp in samples:
    others=[c for c in samples if c!=smp]
    priv=(piv[smp]>0)&(piv[others].max(axis=1)==0)
    sel=piv[priv]
    af=(sel[smp]/dep.loc[sel.index,smp])
    n4=sel[smp]>=4
    bins={'03-05':(0.03,0.05),'05-10':(0.05,0.10),'10-20':(0.10,0.20),'20-30':(0.20,0.30),'30-60':(0.30,0.60)}
    line=[]
    for k,(lo,hi) in bins.items():
        m=n4&(af>=lo)&(af<hi)
        line.append(f'{k}:{m.sum()}')
    # also without >=4
    line2=[]
    for k,(lo,hi) in bins.items():
        m=(af>=lo)&(af<hi)&(sel[smp]>=2)
        line2.append(f'{k}:{m.sum()}')
    print(smp,'altfrag>=4 ',' '.join(line),'   altfrag>=2',' '.join(line2))
    for k,(lo,hi) in bins.items():
        m=n4&(af>=lo)&(af<hi)
        if m.sum():
            types=[f'{i[1]}>{i[2]}' for i in sel[m].index]
            print('   ',k,types)

def canon_ins(p,ins):
    g=0
    while p>0 and ins and ins[-1]==refseq[p-1] and g<60:
        ins=ins[-1]+ins[:-1]; p-=1; g+=1
    return p,ins
def canon_del(p,l):
    g=0
    while p>0 and l>0 and refseq[p-1]==refseq[p+l-1] and g<60:
        p-=1; g+=1
    return p,refseq[p:p+l]
# collect events per sample
ev={}
for s in samples:
    bam=pysam.AlignmentFile(f'{W}/bam/{s}.bam')
    fr=collections.defaultdict(lambda: collections.defaultdict(int))
    cov=collections.defaultdict(set)   # anchor position -> fragments with aligned base there
    keys=set()
    for r in bam.fetch('chr22_panel'):
        if r.is_unmapped or r.is_secondary or r.is_supplementary or r.is_qcfail or r.is_duplicate: continue

        fid=r.query_name.split()[0]
        rp=set()

        fr[fid]['bases']=fr[fid].get('bases',set())|rp
        rpos=r.reference_start; qpos=0; sq=r.query_sequence
        for op,l in r.cigartuples:
            if op==0: rpos+=l; qpos+=l
            elif op==1:
                p,ins=canon_ins(rpos,sq[qpos:qpos+l])
                if 1<=len(ins)<=12: fr[fid][('I',p,ins)]+=1
                qpos+=l
            elif op==2:

                if 1<=len(dele)<=12: fr[fid][('D',p,dele)]+=1
                rpos+=l
            elif op==4: qpos+=l
            elif op==5: rpos+=l
            elif op==3: rpos+=l; qpos+=l
    # aggregate
    allk=collections.Counter()
    for fid,d in fr.items():
        for k,v in d.items():
            if isinstance(k,tuple): allk[k]+=1
    ev[s]={}
    for k in allk:
        sup=set(); r1=0; r2=0
        for fid,d in fr.items():
            if k in d:
                sup.add(fid)
                r1+=d[k]
        t,p,seq=k
        anchor=p-1
        depth=sum(1 for fid,d in fr.items() if anchor in d.get('bases',set()) or fid in sup)
        ev[s][k]={'sup':sup,'depth':depth,'reads':r1,'strand':None}
    # strand split by read is_reverse
    for k in list(ev[s]):
        ev[s][k].pop('reads')
    print(s,'events',len(ev[s]),flush=True)
# merge
allkeys=set()
for s in samples: allkeys.update(ev[s].keys())
rows=[]
for k in sorted(allkeys, key=lambda x:(x[1],x[0])):
    tot=sum(len(ev[s][k]['sup']) for s in samples if k in ev[s])
    if tot<2: continue
    line=[]
    for s in samples:
        d=ev[s].get(k)
        n=len(d['sup']) if d else 0
        dep=d['depth'] if d else 0
        line.append(f'{s[-4:]}:{n}/{dep}={n/dep if dep else 0:.3f}')
    rows.append((k,line))
with open(W+'/indel_stats.txt','w') as fh:

import pickle, numpy as np, pysam, collections, os, json, subprocess
W='/task/work'; OUT='/task/output'; CONTIG='chr22_panel'
samples=[l.strip() for l in open(W+'/samples.txt')]
tp=np.load(W+'/tpos.npy')
candk=pickle.load(open(W+'/cand.pkl','rb'))['cand']
candsites=sorted(set(int(tp[k]) for k in candk))
fa=pysam.FastaFile(W+'/ref.fa'); refseq=fa.fetch(CONTIG).upper()
B='ACGT'
targets=[]
for line in open('/task/input/targets.bed'):
    f=line.split(); targets.append((int(f[1]),int(f[2])))
def in_target(p):
    return any(s0<=p<e0 for s0,e0 in targets)

# SNV fragment-level counts (fragments, not reads)
alt_frags=collections.defaultdict(lambda: collections.defaultdict(set))  # (pos,base)->sample->frags
frags_at=collections.defaultdict(lambda: collections.defaultdict(set))  # pos->sample->frags covering
strand_of=collections.defaultdict(lambda: collections.defaultdict(lambda: [0,0]))
for s in samples:
    fr=pickle.load(open(W+f'/frag_{s}.pkl','rb'))
    for fid,d in fr.items():
        for i,calls in d['base'].items():
            p=candsites[i]; rb=refseq[p]
            altbase=None
            for m,(b,bq,rp) in calls.items():
                if bq<20: continue
                frags_at[p][s].add(fid)
                if b!=rb:
                    ab=B[b]
                    if altbase is None: altbase=ab
                    strand_of[(p,ab)][s][0 if m=='f' else 1]+=1
            if altbase is not None:
                alt_frags[(p,altbase)][s].add(fid)

def af_of(s,p,ab):
    n=len(alt_frags[(p,ab)].get(s,()))
    d=len(frags_at[p].get(s,()))
    return n,d,(n/d if d else 0.0)

# Indels
def canon_ins(p,ins):
    g=0
    while p>0 and ins and ins[-1]==refseq[p-1] and g<80:
        ins=ins[-1]+ins[:-1]; p-=1; g+=1
    return p,ins
def canon_del(p,l):
    g=0
    while p>0 and l>0 and refseq[p-1]==refseq[p+l-1] and g<80:
        p-=1; g+=1
    return p,refseq[p:p+l]
id_sup=collections.defaultdict(lambda: collections.defaultdict(set))
id_cov=collections.defaultdict(lambda: collections.defaultdict(set))
for s in samples:
    bam=pysam.AlignmentFile(f'{W}/bam/{s}.bam')
    anchor=collections.defaultdict(set); ev=collections.defaultdict(set)
    for r in bam.fetch(CONTIG):
        if r.is_unmapped or r.is_secondary or r.is_supplementary or r.is_qcfail or r.is_duplicate: continue
        if r.mapping_quality<20: continue
        fid=r.query_name.split()[0]
        for q,rr in r.get_aligned_pairs(matches_only=True): anchor[rr].add(fid)
        rpos=r.reference_start; qpos=0; sq=r.query_sequence
        for op,l in r.cigartuples:
            if op==0: rpos+=l; qpos+=l
            elif op==1:
                p,ins=canon_ins(rpos,sq[qpos:qpos+l])
                if 1<=len(ins)<=10 and p>0: ev[('I',p,ins)].add(fid)
                qpos+=l
            elif op==2:
                p,dele=canon_del(rpos,l)
                if 1<=len(dele)<=10 and p>0: ev[('D',p,dele)].add(fid)
                rpos+=l
            elif op==4: qpos+=l
            elif op==5: rpos+=l
            elif op==3: rpos+=l; qpos+=l
    for k,fset in ev.items():
        id_sup[k][s]=fset
        id_cov[k][s]=anchor.get(k[1]-1,set())|fset

PAIRS={'PT-0452':('CG24-4187','CG24-1366'),'PT-0740':('CG24-7410','CG24-6425'),'PT-0760':('CG24-9024','CG24-3973')}
FFPE='CG24-9024'
DAMAGE={('C','T'),('G','A'),('C','A'),('G','T')}
MINAF=0.05; MINALT=4

summary={}
with open(OUT+'/pairing.tsv','w') as fh:
    fh.write('patient\ttumour_sample\tnormal_sample\n')
    for pt,(tum,norm) in PAIRS.items():
        fh.write(f'{pt}\t{tum}\t{norm}\n')
records={}
for pt,(tum,norm) in PAIRS.items():
    others=[s for s in samples if s not in (tum,norm)]
    recs=[]
    # SNVs
    for (p,ab),d in sorted(alt_frags.items()):
        tfr=len(d.get(tum,()))
        if tfr<MINALT: continue
        nfr=len(d.get(norm,()))
        t_n,t_d,t_af=af_of(tum,p,ab)
        n_n,n_d,n_af=af_of(norm,p,ab)
        if t_af<MINAF: continue
        if nfr>2 or n_af>=0.02: continue
        if any(len(d.get(o,()))>2 for o in others): continue
        if not in_target(p): continue
        st=strand_of[(p,ab)][tum]
        if st[0]==0 or st[1]==0:
            if tfr<10:
                report.write(f'STRANDBIAS {pt} {p+1} {refseq[p]}>{ab} af={t_af:.3f} frags={tfr} f/r={st}\n'); continue
        if pt=='PT-0760' and t_af<0.30 and (refseq[p],ab) in DAMAGE:
            report.write(f'FFPEART {pt} {p+1} {refseq[p]}>{ab} af={t_af:.3f} frags={tfr}\n'); continue
        recs.append((p+1, refseq[p], ab, t_af, tfr, t_d, 'snv', None))
    # indels
    for k,per_s in id_sup.items():
        t=len(per_s.get(tum,()))
        if t<MINALT: continue
        dep=len(id_cov[k].get(tum,()))
        af=t/dep if dep else 0
        if af<MINAF: continue
        if len(per_s.get(norm,()))>0: continue
        if any(len(per_s.get(o,()))>2 for o in others): continue
        typ,pos0,seq=k
        if not in_target(pos0): continue
        if typ=='I':
            REF=refseq[pos0-1]; ALT=refseq[pos0-1]+seq; POS=pos0
        else:
            REF=refseq[pos0-1:pos0+len(seq)]; ALT=refseq[pos0-1]; POS=pos0
        recs.append((POS,REF,ALT,af,t,dep,'indel',f'{typ}|{pos0}|{seq}'))
    recs.sort()
    records[pt]=recs
    report.write(f'### {pt} {tum} {norm}: n_snv={sum(1 for r in recs if r[6]=="snv")} n_indel={sum(1 for r in recs if r[6]=="indel")}\n')
    for r in recs:
        report.write(f'  {r[0]} {r[1]}>{r[2]} AF={r[3]:.3f} alt={r[4]}/{r[5]} {r[6]} {r[7]}\n')
    hdr=[]
    hdr.append('##fileformat=VCFv4.2')
    hdr.append(f'##reference=file:///task/input/reference/ref.fa')
    hdr.append(f'##contig=<ID={CONTIG},length={len(refseq)}>')
    hdr.append('##FILTER=<ID=PASS,Description="Somatic variant passing all filters">')
    hdr.append('##INFO=<ID=AF,Number=1,Type=Float,Description="Fraction of tumour DNA fragments covering the site carrying the alternate allele">')
    hdr.append('##INFO=<ID=ALT_FRAGS,Number=1,Type=Integer,Description="Number of tumour fragments supporting the alternate allele">')
    hdr.append('##INFO=<ID=FRAG_DEPTH,Number=1,Type=Integer,Description="Number of tumour fragments covering the site">')
    hdr.append('##INFO=<ID=TYPE,Number=1,Type=String,Description="snv or indel">')
    hdr.append('##FORMAT=<ID=GT,Number=1,Type=String,Description="Genotype">')
    hdr.append('##FORMAT=<ID=AD,Number=R,Type=Integer,Description="Allelic depths of tumour fragments">')
    hdr.append('##FORMAT=<ID=DP,Number=1,Type=Integer,Description="Tumour fragment depth">')
    hdr.append(f'#CHROM\tPOS\tID\tREF\tALT\tQUAL\tFILTER\tINFO\tFORMAT\t{tum}')
    with open(f'{W}/{pt}.raw.vcf','w') as fh:
        fh.write('\n'.join(hdr)+'\n')
        for (POS,REF,ALT,af,tfr,dep,typ,extra) in recs:
            fh.write(f'{CONTIG}\t{POS}\t.\t{REF}\t{ALT}\t.\tPASS\tAF={af:.4f};ALT_FRAGS={tfr};FRAG_DEPTH={dep};TYPE={typ}\tGT:AD:DP\t.:{dep-tfr},{tfr}:{dep}\n')
report.close()
print('raw vcfs written')
for pt in PAIRS: print(pt, len(records[pt]))

def canon_ins(p,ins):

    while p>0 and ins and ins[-1]==refseq[p-1] and g<80:

    return p,ins
def canon_del(p,l):

    return p,refseq[p:p+l]

        for op,l in r.cigartuples:

            elif op==1:

                if 1<=len(ins)<=10 and p>0:
